answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token as a bond before its messages can earn reputation; the bond stays at risk through a challenge window, and proven fraud burns it. A Sybil attacker can still mint many identities, but cannot cheaply mint their influence: each one needs capital that remains illiquid and may be destroyed. This makes attacks costly rather than impossible. A wharf’s entry ledger, an opal bond, and an anchor against instant exit capture the mechanism’s parts.
